name: ISO7321CDR
title: Dual-channel 25 Mbps capacitive digital isolators, 3000 VRMS
summary: The ISO7320 and ISO7321 pass two logic signals across a silicon-dioxide capacitive isolation barrier rated 3000 VRMS for one minute (UL 1577) and 4242 VPK (VDE). ISO7320 sends both channels the same way, ISO7321 one each way. Each side runs from 3 V to 5.5 V, inputs are TTL-level with a glitch filter, and the C and FC suffixes set the output a lost input defaults to: high or low. They run up to 25 Mbps with 33 ns typical delay at 5 V, in a narrow SOIC-8 rated -40 °C to 125 °C.

circuits.title: Isolated 4-20 mA current-loop transmitter
circuits.description: A 3.3 V supply on the controller side runs an MSP430G2132 (U1) and the VCC1 side of the ISO7321 (U2), and also powers an SN6501 transformer driver (U3). U3 drives the primary of a 1:1.3 centre-tapped transformer T1 whose centre tap sits on the 3.3 V rail; two MBR0520L Schottky diodes rectify the secondary against its grounded centre tap, and a TPS76333 regulator (U4) makes 3.3VISO from that. 3.3VISO feeds VCC2 of the isolator and the DAC161P997 (U5) at VA, and its VD pin through a 20 Ω resistor. U5's DBACK reaches controller pin P3.0 through isolator channel A (INA to OUTA); P3.1 drives U5's DIN through channel B. U5's BASE pin drives an NPN transistor Q1; its collector is LOOP+, its emitter returns to the isolated ground through 22 Ω, and OUT is LOOP-. 0.1 µF and 1 µF sit across the loop terminals, three 2.2 nF capacitors hang on C1-C3, and LOW and ERRLVL are grounded. Every supply pin has 0.1 µF to its own ground.
notes: Pin numbers: U1 DVCC 2, DVSS 4, XOUT 5, XIN 6, P3.0 11, P3.1 12; U3 VCC 2, GND 4 and 5, D1 1, D2 3; U4 IN 1, GND 2, EN 3, OUT 5; U5 COMA 1, COMD 2, VD 3, DIN 4, DBACK 5, ERRLVL 8, OUT 9, LOW 10, C3 12, C2 13, C1 14, VA 15, BASE 16.
The loop leaves on a twisted pair.

circuits.title: Switching characteristic test circuit
circuits.description: One channel is driven from a pulse generator into its input, which carries a 50 Ω termination to ground; the output drives CL = 15 pF to ground, and VI and VO are read across the two. The generator runs at a pulse rate of 50 kHz or less, 50% duty cycle, rise and fall of 3 ns or less, 50 Ω source. The 50 Ω terminator serves only the generator. CL counts the probe and fixture capacitance and is held within ±20%. Delays are timed between the 50% points of VI and VO; rise and fall between 10% and 90% of VO.
notes: Channel B of the ISO7321 stands for any channel; both grounds share one return.

circuits.title: Fail-safe output delay-time test circuit
circuits.description: The input-side supply is the stimulus: VI is applied to VCC and stepped down to 0 V while the input is held at 0 V on devices without the F suffix and at VCC on those with it. The output drives CL = 15 pF (probe and fixture included, ±20%) and tfs runs from VI passing 2.7 V to VO crossing 50% on its way to the fail-safe level, high (fs high) or low (fs low).

circuits.title: Common-mode transient immunity test circuit
circuits.description: A common-mode source VCM is connected between the input-side ground GNDI and the output-side ground GNDO. Switch S1 holds the input at VCCI or at GNDI. Each supply has 0.1 µF ±1% to its own ground, and the output drives CL = 15 pF (probe and fixture included, ±20%) to GNDO. The part passes when the output holds its VOH or VOL level steadily through the transient.
notes: Channel B of the ISO7321 stands for any channel.

operation.text: ISO7320 carries both channels from side 1 to side 2; ISO7321 carries channel B from side 1 to side 2 and channel A back from side 2 to side 1. Parts with the F in the suffix go low when the input side loses power or the input is left open; parts without it go high.

Each channel crosses a silicon-dioxide capacitive barrier along two paths. Edges from 100 kbps up to 25 Mbps travel a high-frequency path: the input is made differential, RC networks turn each edge into a short pulse above or below a reference, and a comparator whose threshold follows the expected next edge restores the logic level. Content from 100 kbps down to DC is pulse-width modulated onto an internal oscillator carrier, sent over a low-frequency path and low-pass filtered on the far side. A decision block watches the time between edges and hands the output multiplexer to the low-frequency path when edges stop coming.

The inputs have a built-in filter that ignores short glitches; the suppression time is about 20.5 ns to 27.5 ns over temperature. Input pulses must be 40 ns or longer. Inputs have TTL thresholds with about 450 mV of hysteresis.

Each side runs from its own 3 V to 5.5 V supply, so a 3.3 V side and a 5 V side can be joined directly. A supply counts as powered at 3 V or more and as off at 2.1 V or less; the undervoltage threshold is about 2.43 V to 2.47 V rising and 2.35 V falling. When the input side is off, the output takes its default level within about 7.5 µs; when the output side is off its output is undetermined.

Each input has clamp diodes to VCCI and ground, a 500 Ω series resistor, and a 5 µA current source that pulls the input up to VCCI on parts without F or down to ground on F parts. Each output is a CMOS stage with a 40 Ω series resistor and clamp diodes to VCCO and to ground.

The part isolates single-ended CMOS or TTL lines and follows no interface standard of its own. It goes between a controller (a microcontroller or UART) and a converter or line transceiver, whatever the bus.

Inside the chip: strong ESD cells on every signal pin and on the bond pads between the two dies, with low-resistance ties to supply and ground, a barrier capacitor built to take ESD, EFT and surge, large on-chip decoupling, guard rings between PMOS and NMOS devices against parasitic SCR latch-up, and fully differential internal signalling that keeps common-mode current across the barrier low.

Put a 0.1 µF capacitor on VCC1 and on VCC2, each as close to its pin as possible. Where only a primary-side supply exists, the secondary side can be powered from a transformer driver such as the SN6501.

Standard FR-4 suits boards with signals below 150 Mbps (edges slower than 1 ns) and traces up to 10 inches; it meets UL94-V0 and has lower high-frequency loss and moisture uptake than cheaper laminates.

Use at least four layers, top to bottom: fast signals, ground plane, power plane, slow signals. Fast traces on top avoid vias; the ground plane under them sets their impedance and gives the return current a low-inductance path; the power plane next to ground adds about 100 pF/in² of bypass capacitance; slow control lines on the bottom tolerate vias. In the recommended stack the layers are 10 mil, 40 mil and 10 mil apart in FR-4 with εr about 4.5, and the area under the isolator between the two sides is kept clear of planes, traces, pads and vias. More layers should be added as a second power and ground pair so the stack stays symmetrical.
Isolation barrier life is over 25 years. Common-mode transient immunity is 65 kV/µs typical at 5 V and 50 kV/µs at 3.3 V, 25 kV/µs minimum.
At 25 Mbps and 25 °C the output eye is wide open at both 5 V and 3.3 V; peak-to-peak jitter stays near 100 ps to 145 ps across data rate.
